What they did well:
- Your SQL syntax is correct and the query is well-structured. 
- You've used the SUM function correctly to aggregate the total rental fees for each movie.
- You've also used the GROUP BY clause correctly to group the results by movie name.

Any corrections or improvements:
- Your query seems to be perfect for the given task. However, it would be a good idea to include an ORDER BY clause to sort the results. This could be either in ascending or descending order of Total_Sales, depending on your requirements. Here's how you can do it:

```
SELECT 
    Movie_Name, 
    SUM(Rental_Fee) AS Total_Sales
FROM 
    Movie_Rentals
GROUP BY 
    Movie_Name
ORDER BY 
    Total_Sales DESC;
```

Pro tips to go further:
- You might want to consider handling NULL values in your query. If Rental_Fee has NULL values, the SUM function will ignore them. If you want to treat NULL as 0, you can use the COALESCE function like this: SUM(COALESCE(Rental_Fee, 0)).
- If you want to filter your results based on the aggregated data, you can use the HAVING clause. For example, if you want to see only those movies that have made more than $1000, you can add `HAVING SUM(Rental_Fee) > 1000` after the GROUP BY clause.
- Always remember to use meaningful aliases for your columns, especially when using aggregate functions. You've done this well with "Total_Sales". This makes your results easier to understand.
